note: The peer-controlled KEXINIT algorithm list is parsed into algs and used to decide whether strict KEX is enabled.
A match on the attacker-controlled list sets the session into strict-KEX mode.
Strict-KEX packet ordering requires the next packet type to equal the expected required type; this obligation is violated when an unexpected packet is accepted for further processing.
The decrypted packet payload is forwarded into packet processing after the transport layer assembles it.
The vulnerable path is triggered by the strict-KEX agreement check on the peer-supplied algorithm string, which leads to later packet handling under strict mode.
